mechanism_narrative: The recent pullback in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT reflects weaker weekday circulation, which should continue to suppress discretionary shopping trips and keep RETAIL_REC below its prior four-week average over the next month.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from -12.6 to -20.9 while TRANSIT stayed around -29 to -37 over the snapshot window
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC averages above its last-4-week mean over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remaining depressed, this mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM turns back toward baseline after a decline, nearby trip chaining releases latent out-of-home demand and lifts RETAIL_REC within one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises by at least 5 points from its prior weekly mean after being negative
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM moved from -8.4 to -1.1 in the latest week after two negative weeks
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM rebounds above its prior week but RETAIL_REC does not improve within 14 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous drop in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES below their recent ranges signals renewed mobility suppression; under that regime, retail activity falls further over the next four weeks as commuting-based incidental shopping disappears.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT stays below -25 and WORKPLACES stays below -25 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT was -31.3 and WORKPLACES was -35.1 in t-1w, with both still negative in t-0w
failure_condition: If both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain below -25 for two weeks but RETAIL_REC rises relative to the last four weeks, reject the mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: A sharper than usual rise in RESIDENTIAL activity indicates people are staying home more, which reduces discretionary store visits and pushes RETAIL_REC down over the next one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL is at least 10 points above its own recent four-week average
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL remains elevated at 11.1 after 7.1, 14.9, and 12.9 in prior weeks
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL stays elevated but RETAIL_REC improves within 7 to 14 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS after a deep decline signals renewed local leisure activity and willingness to leave home, which should spill over into higher RETAIL_REC within four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises for two consecutive weeks after being below -20
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -28.0 to -25.1 after a low of -27.1 and -17.4 earlier
failure_condition: If PARKS stabilizes or rises for two weeks and RETAIL_REC remains below its previous four-week mean, the mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL move in opposite directions, household time is being reallocated from errands to home-based activity, which weakens discretionary retail demand over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stayed near baseline while RESIDENTIAL remained above 10 in the latest weeks
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL diverge as specified but RETAIL_REC does not soften within 14 days, reject the hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT recovers first while WORKPLACES stays depressed, mobility is returning for nonwork purposes rather than commuting, and retail should improve only with a short lag as weekend and evening shopping resumes.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by at least 5 points while WORKPLACES remains below -20
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -36.7 to -29.0 while WORKPLACES improved from -47.6 to -20.9
failure_condition: If TRANSIT improves while WORKPLACES stays weak but RETAIL_REC does not rise within 7 days, the hypothesis is false.

mechanism_narrative: A combined rebound in PARKS and RESIDENTIAL after winter suppression marks holiday-at-home substitution ending; that shift should raise retail demand over the next month as outing intensity normalizes.
candidate_trigger: PARKS increases by 5 points and RESIDENTIAL falls by 2 points from their recent means
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS and RESIDENTIAL have moved in opposite directions across the snapshot window
failure_condition: If PARKS rebounds and RESIDENTIAL cools but RETAIL_REC remains below its prior four-week mean over the next 28 days, the mechanism is rejected.
